name: Validate and introduce new tests
summary: When a new or changed test is approved, a validation analyst in quality assurance plans the studies, technologists run precision, method comparison, reportable range and reference interval experiments, and the medical director approves the report. The LIS team then builds the test, technologists write the procedure and are trained, the test is enrolled in proficiency testing and, if needed, added to the laboratory licence before go-live. Most of the five months or so a test takes is waiting: for reagents and vendor installation, for enough patient samples, for outside comparison results, for approvals and above all for the LIS build backlog.

baseline.org_archetype: A large Canadian community laboratory company with regional laboratories, specialty and genetics laboratories, and a central quality department with a validation team.
baseline.notes: Most cases are verifications of licensed commercial kits on existing analysers; a minority are full validations of modified or laboratory-developed methods in specialty and genetics laboratories.

trigger: A new test or method change is approved by strategy, sales or a companion diagnostics program and handed to the validation team.
end_state: The test is live: validation report and procedure approved, LIS build accepted, staff trained, proficiency testing in place and change control released; or the project is stopped because performance is unacceptable.

volume.seasonality: Bunched around analyser platform changes and the annual menu plan.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file process map (volume estimate).

The company's system validation analysts sit in quality assurance and validate new assay methods, products and equipment (s_dyn_sysval). FTE share is the author's estimate from hands-on time; the rest of the 8 analysts work on LIS change validation.

roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

steps.name: Open the validation project from the approved request
steps.description: The validation analyst receives the approved new test request with its intended use, expected volume, platform and chosen kit, opens a change control record in the quality management system and classifies the work as verification of an unmodified licensed kit or full validation of a modified or laboratory-developed method.

error.defect_description: A modified method is classed as a simple verification.

evidence.note: Change control is part of the company QMS (s_dyn_licences); verification is a smaller version of validation (s_ladwig2018). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check licensing and funding status
steps.description: The licensing and regulatory affairs specialist checks whether the test falls within the laboratory's licensed tests in its province, whether a licence amendment will be needed, whether the kit holds a Health Canada device licence and whether the test is insured or will be patient-paid.

error.defect_description: A needed licence amendment is not identified until late.

control.basis: Ontario Laboratory and Specimen Collection Centre Licensing Act and equivalent Quebec and Manitoba licensing: a laboratory performs only the tests its licence covers

evidence.note: Community laboratories are not licensed for some tests and the Ministry had no process to evaluate new tests for funding (s_ag2017); check whether new tests need licensing (s_cln_2012).

steps.name: Draft the validation plan with acceptance criteria
steps.description: The validation analyst chooses the experiments (precision, method comparison, reportable range, detection limit, carry-over, interference and reference interval), sets the number of samples, runs and days for each, and writes acceptance criteria from allowable total error and the manufacturer's claims.

error.defect_description: Acceptance criteria are too loose or the sample range misses a decision level.

evidence.note: Written plan with acceptance criteria and CLSI experiments (s_ladwig2018); sample numbers such as 40 comparison specimens and 20 replicates (s_westgard_mv). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Medical director approves the validation plan
steps.description: The medical director reviews the intended use, the experiments and the acceptance criteria, asks for changes where a clinical decision level is not covered, and approves the plan in the change control record.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Laboratory director responsibility for method selection and validation under ISO 15189 and CAP; plan approval before studies is company policy

evidence.note: Return rate and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Order reagents, calibrators and controls
steps.description: The validation analyst raises purchase requisitions for evaluation kits, calibrators and third-party QC material, and asks the vendor to install the assay application file on the analyser.

error.defect_description: Not enough reagent is ordered for repeat studies.

evidence.note: Estimate volume to order enough reagent and choose QC material (s_cln_2012); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for supplier delivery and assay installation
steps.description: The laboratory waits for the supplier to deliver the reagents and controls and for the vendor's field application specialist to load and check the assay on the analyser.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; back-ordered or imported reagents take longer.

steps.name: Collect and bank patient samples for the studies
steps.description: A technologist pulls leftover de-identified patient specimens from routine work that span the measuring range and decision levels, aliquots and freezes them with a log, and keeps collecting until rare high or positive samples are found.

error.defect_description: Samples cluster in the normal range.

evidence.note: At least 40 patient specimens spanning the range (s_westgard_mv); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run precision and reportable range studies
steps.description: Technologists run control and patient pools in replicate across several days and operators for precision, and a dilution series of five or more levels in triplicate for the reportable range, recording lot numbers and maintenance as they go.

error.defect_description: A run is done with an expired calibrator.

evidence.note: At least 20 replicate determinations on two levels and at least 5 specimens in triplicate for reportable range; several analysts give realistic imprecision (s_westgard_mv). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run the method comparison and send split samples out
steps.description: Technologists test the banked specimens on the new method and the current or reference method within two hours of each other, a few each day over the study period, and ship split samples to an outside laboratory when no in-house comparator exists.

error.defect_description: A sample pair is run too far apart and gives a false bias.

next.condition: comparison done by an outside laboratory

evidence.note: At least 40 specimens, 2 to 5 a day over the replication period (s_westgard_mv); the share needing an outside comparator is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for comparison results from the outside laboratory
steps.description: The split samples travel to the outside laboratory, are tested in its normal workflow and the results come back by report or file for matching to the in-house results.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Verify the reference interval
steps.description: A technologist tests about 20 specimens from healthy donors or suitable banked samples and checks that no more than a few fall outside the manufacturer's or literature reference interval, or flags that a new interval must be established.

error.defect_description: Donors do not represent the patient population.

evidence.note: Verify reference intervals (s_westgard_mv) per CLSI EP28 (s_ladwig2018); the 20-specimen count is the author's knowledge of EP28 verification practice.

steps.name: Analyse the data against acceptance criteria
steps.description: The validation analyst enters the raw data into the statistics workbook, calculates imprecision, bias, regression, linearity and total error, compares each with the acceptance criteria and decides whether the method passes, needs troubleshooting and repeat runs, or should be abandoned.

error.defect_description: A calculation error hides a failing bias.

next.condition: fails a criterion: troubleshoot with the vendor and repeat

evidence.note: Judge performance against allowable error; real methods still have real problems (s_westgard_mv). Failure and abandonment shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the validation report
steps.description: The validation analyst writes the report with the plan, raw data references, statistics, deviations, conclusions, reference interval, reportable range and QC rules to use, and attaches it to the change control record.

error.defect_description: Missing raw data reference or unsigned worksheet.

evidence.note: A validation summary is written at the end (s_ladwig2018); hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Quality specialist reviews the report and records
steps.description: A quality assurance specialist checks the report against the plan, traces a sample of results back to instrument printouts, confirms lot numbers and dates and that every deviation is explained, and returns gaps to the analyst.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Medical director approves the validation report
steps.description: The medical director reviews the report, the reference interval and the clinical comments, decides on critical limits and reporting rules, and signs the report so that patient testing may start once the build and training are done.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and CAP: the laboratory director approves method validation before patient results are reported; accreditation (ISO 15189 Plus, CAP, MANQAP) required for the provincial laboratory licence

evidence.note: Results may not be released before performance characteristics are established (s_ladwig2018); the process map names medical director approval. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Submit the LIS build request with the validation report
steps.description: The validation analyst completes the LIS change request: test and result codes, specimen requirements, units, reference intervals by age and sex, critical limits, reportable range, report comments, billing code and order mappings for EMRs and OLIS, and attaches the approved report.

error.defect_description: A reference interval or unit is keyed wrongly on the request.

evidence.note: Notify IT of reference intervals, cut-offs, critical values and comments (s_cln_2012); these are built into the LIS (s_cln_2026). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the bench procedure
steps.description: A technologist writes the procedure for the new test in the document control module, covering specimen requirements, calibration, QC rules, analysis, result review, reporting and troubleshooting, using the validation report and kit insert.

error.defect_description: The procedure differs from the validated settings.

evidence.note: Write procedures for each new process (s_cln_2012, s_westgard_mv); hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the LIS build and its system validation
steps.description: The LIS and integration team builds the test, rules and interface mappings and the validation team tests the build under the LIS change process; the new test waits in that backlog.
outputs: LIS build ready for user acceptance

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the process map notes that LIS backlogs delay new tests.

steps.name: Medical director approves the procedure
steps.description: The medical director reviews the draft procedure in the document control workflow and approves it so it can be issued to the bench on the go-live date.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: ISO 15189 document control: procedures approved by an authorised person before use; accreditation (ISO 15189 Plus, CAP, MANQAP) required for the provincial laboratory licence

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Laboratory user acceptance of the built test
steps.description: The charge technologist orders the test on test patients, runs it through the analyser and middleware, checks worklists, flags, reference ranges, comments and the report as it appears in eResults, and sends defects back to the LIS team.
inputs: LIS build ready for user acceptance
outputs: user acceptance sign-off or defect list

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: defects returned to the LIS team

evidence.note: User acceptance testing by front-line staff and fix-and-retest before go-live (s_cln_2026); the defect share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Train technologists and record competency
steps.description: The charge technologist trains each technologist who will run the test on the procedure and analyser, observes them testing samples, and records training and competency in the quality management system before they report patient results.

error.defect_description: A technologist on another shift is missed.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and CAP: staff are trained and assessed as competent before performing patient testing; accreditation (ISO 15189 Plus, CAP, MANQAP) required for the provincial laboratory licence

evidence.note: Hands-on training for new tests (s_cln_2012); hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Enrol the test in proficiency testing
steps.description: A quality assurance specialist adds the test to the laboratory's proficiency testing subscriptions with the provider, or sets up an alternative assessment such as inter-laboratory sample exchange where no PT program exists.
outputs: PT enrolment or alternative assessment plan

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Ontario quality management program: licensed laboratories must take part in proficiency testing for the tests they perform

evidence.note: PT participation is required for licensed laboratories (s_ag2017); enrol each test or use an alternative (s_cln_2012); EQA covers all assays (s_dyn_licences). The licensing share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: File the licence amendment
steps.description: The regulatory affairs specialist prepares and files the application to add the test or test class to the laboratory licence, with the validation summary and director attestation the ministry requires.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Ontario Laboratory and Specimen Collection Centre Licensing Act and provincial equivalents

evidence.note: Licences are test-specific (s_ag2017, s_cln_2012); the content and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the licence amendment
steps.description: The provincial licensing office reviews the application and issues the amended licence; the test cannot go live for patients until it arrives.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Release change control and set the go-live date
steps.description: A quality assurance specialist checks that the validation report, procedure, LIS build sign-off, training, PT enrolment and any licence are all complete, closes the change control record and confirms the go-live date with the laboratory and client communications.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Change control within the company QMS required by ISO 15189 Plus and CAP

evidence.note: Change control is part of the company QMS (s_dyn_licences); notify clients before go-live (s_cln_2012). Times are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Study fails acceptance criteria
exceptions.description: Bias or imprecision exceeds the criteria; the technologists troubleshoot with the vendor and repeat the studies.

exceptions.name: Project abandoned
exceptions.description: The method cannot meet the criteria and the request is closed.

exceptions.name: Outside comparison laboratory
exceptions.description: No in-house comparator exists, so split samples go to an outside laboratory.

exceptions.name: LIS build defects
exceptions.description: User acceptance finds a wrong range, flag or report format and the build goes back to the LIS team.

exceptions.name: Licence amendment
exceptions.description: The test is outside the current licence and must be added before go-live.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from approved request to go-live
benchmarks.population: Mixed verifications and validations in a community and specialty laboratory network

evidence.note: Sources bound the range: verification of licensed kits under an accredited flexible scope in under two weeks of study time (s_lefeuvre2020) and up to 12 months to develop and validate a laboratory-developed test (s_thermo2022). The p50 and p90, which include procurement, approvals, LIS build and training, are the author's estimate.

benchmarks.unit: minimum patient specimens for a comparison of methods

pain_points.description: New tests wait weeks in the LIS build backlog after validation is finished.

evidence.note: The organisation file process map states that LIS backlogs delay new tests; durations are the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Validation studies run around routine bench work, so sample banking and multi-day runs stretch out, and rare high or positive samples take longest to find.

evidence.note: Analytical validation is the most variable phase because of limited technical resources.

pain_points.description: Medical director approvals for plan, report and procedure each queue behind clinical duties.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Reference intervals, units and critical limits are re-keyed from the report to the LIS request and build, a common source of build defects caught only at user acceptance.

evidence.note: Reference intervals and critical values must be passed to IT and built into the LIS.

sources.title: Method validation: the real world applications
sources.supports: Define allowable total error, plan experiments and schedule staff time; reportable range with at least 5 specimens in triplicate; replication with at least 20 determinations on two control levels (reduced studies over at least ten days); comparison of methods with at least 40 patient specimens (20 for reduced studies); detection limit with a blank and spiked specimen 20 times each; interference studies; verify reference intervals; then write the procedure, training material and QC rules.

sources.title: Practical considerations for implementing a new lab analyzer (J. Shaw)
sources.supports: Team with bench, senior technical and LIS staff; realistic and ideal go-live dates; notify IT of new tests, reference intervals, cut-offs, critical values and comments; check whether new tests need licensing; choose QC and quality goals; enrol each test in EQA or PT; write procedures; hands-on training; notify clients before go-live; post-go-live review.

sources.title: Establishing and implementing LDTs utilizing the Test Life Cycle Model (P. Ladwig)
sources.supports: Establishment (feasibility, development, validation with a written plan and acceptance criteria: precision EP05, accuracy EP09, detection EP17, specificity EP07, stability EP25, measuring and reference intervals EP06 and EP28, validation summary) and implementation (preliminary evaluation, verification on a smaller scale with a written plan, launch, maintenance, retirement).

sources.title: Practical approach to method verification and validation under accreditation using a flexible scope in molecular virology (Lefeuvre et al.)
sources.publisher: Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (record read through Europe PMC)
sources.supports: Verification of three CE/IVD viral load assays on a new platform under an ISO 15189 flexible scope could be set up in less than two weeks; repeatability, method comparison (R2 0.96) and measurement uncertainty studies.

sources.title: 7 things to know before establishing an LDT (M. Gandhi)
sources.supports: Depending on the technology it can take up to 12 months to develop and validate a laboratory developed test; the analytical validation period is the most variable and often runs longer than planned because of limited technical resources.

sources.title: 2017 Annual Report, Section 3.07: Laboratory Services in the Health Sector
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Read from the text copy saved under scratch by earlier work. All licensed laboratories must follow the provincial quality management program of accreditation and proficiency testing (Institute for Quality Management in Healthcare, now Accreditation Canada Diagnostics): on-site assessment every four years, a self-assessment two years after the previous visit (ISO 15189 Plus labs get a surveillance visit at two years instead), next visit confirmed about 90 days ahead. 2012-2016: about 800 non-conformances a year, average 15 per assessment visit (8 to 28 by region), conformance about 97% against more than 400 requirements; most common categories point-of-care testing (17%), laboratory systems for tracking issues with testing (16%), equipment and supplies (12%). Proficiency testing error rate below 1% (0.04% pathology to 1.8% bacteriology). CAP and the Joint Commission make unannounced visits. Community laboratories are not licensed to perform some tests; the Ministry had no process to evaluate new tests for the Schedule of Benefits. Community specimen rejection rates 0.9% and 0.2% in 2016/17.

sources.title: Manager, System Validations (job posting, Brampton)
sources.supports: Leads the System Validation Analysts in quality assurance, who validate information system changes for new assay methods, products and equipment across the LIS (AS400, Omnitech, national order entry, middleware, LabDirector, MedLab) and result outputs (EMRs, eResults, OLIS); product owner of the electronic QMS for document, occurrence and equipment management; supports external inspections by regulators, accreditation bodies and clients; internal audits and periodic reviews of information systems. Salary CAD 72,000 to 90,000.

sources.title: Licences and quality commitment
sources.supports: Accreditations by laboratory: Accreditation Canada ISO 15189 (Brampton, London, Ottawa, Peterborough), CAP (Brampton, London, Ottawa, Winnipeg, Impact Genetics), SCC ISO 15189 and ISO/IEC 17025 (Laval, Brampton, London, Edmonton), SAMHSA (London, Edmonton), MANQAP (Winnipeg), provincial licences. QMS components include management review, internal corporate quality audits, preventive and corrective action programs, equipment validation, change control and computerized systems validation, document and record control, and external quality assessment for all assays (CAP, QMP-LS, Healthmetrix).

sources.title: Navigating the risks and benefits of implementing a new laboratory information system (Tsui, Venner)
sources.supports: LIS build covers tests, panels, reflex rules, reportable ranges, reference intervals, critical values and specimen requirements plus instrument and middleware interfaces; system testing of individual builds, interfaces and order-to-report workflows; user acceptance testing by front-line staff; issues documented and fixed before go-live with retesting; governance needed for requests that affect laboratory workflows.

assumptions: The LIS build and its formal system validation are counted in it-lis-change; this workflow waits for them (s18) and adds only the laboratory's user acceptance (s20).
Technologist steps use the core laboratory technologist role; specialty and genetics validations would use reference or molecular technologists at similar cost.
About 15% of new tests need a licence amendment and 40% need an outside comparison laboratory; both shares are the author's estimate.
The validation report is handed to it-lis-change at s16, before go-live; the interface lists it under the 'live' outcome because abandoned projects never send one.
Hands-on time is about 100 to 110 hours per test, typical for verification of a commercial kit; full validations of laboratory-developed tests can take several times more.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (hourly wage times 1.35).
